audit_period: 28 September to 2 October 2026 (ten sessions: snack and lunch, Monday to Friday)
survey_period: October 2025, 105 respondents. The October 2026 dates on the PDF printouts are print dates, not collection dates.

bin_rubric.R: 5 or more misplaced items, or serious wet food or liquid on recyclables

litter_rubric.R: 16 or more pieces, or a concentrated pile

limitations: Grades are visual estimates by student auditors during about five minutes per check, so they can differ between auditors.
Auditors checked the worst-looking bin cluster in each zone. Results describe those checks, not all campus bins or all waste.
Repeated checks can include the same bins and the same remaining litter. 60 bin checks are not 60 different bins.
Grades are categories, not item counts. They cannot be turned into item percentages, and Red implies no minimum count.
Green does not mean zero litter or perfect sorting. Some Green organic-bin grades were given to empty bins.
The audit standard describes a surface scan, while the auditor guide says to lift lids. The records do not show which was used each time.
Friday was a half day, so conditions differed from other days.
The survey (multiple selections allowed on the location question) and the audit use different measures about a year apart. No change over time is calculated.
The basketball hub was not a separate survey location option, so no survey figure is shown for it.
